title: The Blur Beyond the Numbers

patient.name: Ms Tan Wei Ling
patient.presenting_complaint: Glare and haloes at night despite 'perfect' glasses; referred for wavefront aberrometry before a refractive surgery consult

history.hpc: Ms Tan is spectacle- and contact-lens-corrected to 6/6 but complains of night-time glare, starbursts around headlights, and difficulty with fine screen work in dim light. Her subjective refraction is stable. She is being worked up for possible refractive surgery and needs objective measurement of her total (lower- and higher-order) aberrations.
history.pmhx: Myopia since teens. No prior ocular surgery. No dry eye diagnosis.
history.social_hx: Wears soft contact lenses on weekends; drives at night.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Clear corneas, no significant tear-film instability at the slit lamp; pupils equal and reactive
examination_findings.fundus: Not assessed — not indicated for this measurement

investigations.aberrometry: Wavefront aberrometry captured with a good-quality Hartmann-Shack image over a well-centred, adequately sized pupil. Lower-order aberrations match her manifest refraction (myopic astigmatism). Higher-order aberrations show elevated spherical aberration and coma, larger over the scotopic (dilated) pupil — consistent with her night-time glare/haloes.
investigations.quality_checks: Contact lenses removed beforehand; measurement repeated to confirm reproducibility; alignment and fixation confirmed; ambient light lowered to obtain the physiological (larger) pupil for night-symptom correlation.

diagnosis: Good-quality wavefront aberrometry showing myopic astigmatism (lower-order) plus elevated higher-order aberrations (spherical aberration and coma) that increase with pupil size — a plausible explanation for her night-time glare and haloes. Findings handed to the ophthalmologist for the refractive surgery decision; the technician does not decide suitability.

immediate: Confirm identity, explain the test, and ensure contact lenses have been out long enough before measuring
Seat and align the patient; ensure steady fixation and a well-centred pupil
Capture a good-quality wavefront (Hartmann-Shack) image and check the acquisition/quality indices before accepting it
Repeat the measurement to confirm reproducibility
Measure under lowered ambient light so the larger (scotopic) pupil is captured, since her symptoms are nocturnal
Recognise that lower-order aberrations should track her manifest refraction; flag the elevated higher-order aberrations
follow_up: Document the total, lower-order, and higher-order aberrations with pupil size and image-quality notes
Hand the report to the ophthalmologist for the refractive-surgery decision (out of technician scope)
Retain the images for comparison at follow-up
patient_education: Explain in plain terms that the test maps how light focuses through her eye, beyond what glasses measure
Reassure that the glare/haloes she describes fit the higher-order pattern seen
Advise that the doctor will use these results to advise on suitability and options

key_points: Elicits the specific visual symptoms (glare, haloes, night difficulty) and their context (driving, dim screen work)
Confirms stable subjective refraction and reason for referral (refractive surgery work-up)
Checks contact lens wear and ensures adequate lens-free interval before measurement
Screens for confounders such as dry eye that degrade wavefront quality
Aligns the patient and obtains steady fixation with a well-centred pupil
Captures a good-quality wavefront image and checks acquisition/quality indices before accepting
Repeats the measurement to confirm reproducibility
Captures under lowered ambient light to obtain the scotopic pupil relevant to night symptoms
Confirms lower-order aberrations correspond to the manifest refraction
Identifies elevated higher-order aberrations (spherical aberration, coma)
Links the pupil-size dependence to the patient's nocturnal symptoms
Stays within scope — measures and reports, does not decide surgical suitability
Documents total/lower-/higher-order aberrations with pupil size and image quality
Hands the report to the ophthalmologist for decision-making
